app.name: JobSheet
app.tagline: Collect job ads from anywhere. Get a spreadsheet you actually own.

nav.searchHint: Pick sources, say what you want

search.title: Search
search.lede: Every source below is a public feed or a public API. No account, no key, nothing behind a login.
search.keywordsHelp: Groups are tried in order, and the first one that matches names the job's category.
search.termPlaceholder: Type a word and press Enter
search.noSources: Choose at least one source first.
search.waiting: Waiting for the first source to answer…

results.title: Results
results.lede: Everything collected so far. Your workbook is built from this.
results.empty: No jobs yet. Run a search and they will land here.
results.forgetSure: Forget this job and its history? Nothing else deletes anything in JobSheet.
results.turnedAwayLede: Ads that matched your words but were removed by a rule. Shown so you can see which rule.

designer.title: Sheet designer
designer.lede: The workbook is the product. Arrange it exactly as you want it, and every run writes into that shape.
designer.columnsHelp: Drag to reorder. Rename anything. Add a column of your own for notes the app will never touch.
designer.previewHelp: This is what the first rows of your workbook will look like.
designer.label: Heading
designer.yoursHelp: The app creates this column and then never writes to it.
designer.adopted: Took back {{count}} edit(s) you made in Excel first.
designer.locked: That workbook is open in Excel. Close it and try again.
designer.problems: This design will not work yet
designer.customKeyHelp: A name the app does not recognise becomes your own column.

tracker.title: Tracker
tracker.lede: Drag a card, or use the arrows above a column. Every move is dated, so "when did I apply?" has an answer.
tracker.noHistory: This one has not moved yet.
tracker.boardEmpty: Nothing to track yet. Run a search, then keep what looks worth keeping.

settings.title: Settings
settings.lede: Everything JobSheet keeps, it keeps on this machine, in files you can open.
settings.sourcesLede: Third-party endpoints change without notice. This is the last thing each one actually did.
settings.fairPlayText: JobSheet reads public feeds and public APIs, respects robots.txt, rate-limits itself and identifies itself honestly. It does not log in anywhere and does not touch anything behind an authentication wall.
settings.workbookHint: The spreadsheet you open. Change where it lives, and take it with you.
settings.moveWorkbook: Move the workbook I already have to the new place
settings.moveWorkbookWarning: Without this, the ticks and notes you typed in the old workbook stay in the old workbook. JobSheet will start a new one at the new path.
settings.workbookMoved: Moved. The workbook and everything in it is at the new path.
settings.workbookPointed: Done. JobSheet now writes to the new path.
settings.folderReadOnly: This folder cannot be written to. Pick another one.

letter.title: Application letter
letter.lede: A first draft, filled in from the ad. JobSheet fills the mechanical parts; the words are yours.
letter.pitchPlaceholder: The one paragraph about you that changes per job.

auth.usernameHint: 3-32 characters. Letters, digits, dots, hyphens, underscores.
auth.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. Nothing else is required of it.
auth.localNote: JobSheet runs on this computer and answers nothing but this computer. The password keeps the people who share the machine apart -- it is not an account on anybody's server, and nothing leaves here.
auth.switchToClaim: Take over the search already here

login.title: Sign in
login.lede: Your searches, your spreadsheet, your notes.

register.title: Make your account
register.lede: One minute of questions, then a search that runs.

claim.title: This search is waiting for you
claim.lede: There are jobs, notes and statuses in this JobSheet from before it had accounts. Pick a name and a password and they are yours.

errors.bad_credentials: That username and password do not match.
errors.username_taken: That name is already in use on this computer.
errors.username_invalid: A username is 3-32 characters: a letter or digit first, then letters, digits, dots, hyphens or underscores.
errors.password_too_short: A password needs at least 8 characters.
errors.password_is_username: A password cannot be the same as the username.
errors.too_many_attempts: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
errors.nothing_to_claim: Somebody has already taken that search over.
errors.already_claimed: That account already has a password.
errors.workbook_not_xlsx: A workbook has to be an .xlsx file.
errors.workbook_is_a_folder: That is a folder, not a file.
errors.workbook_folder_missing: There is no folder at that path.

auth.passwordChanged: Changed. Every window has been signed out, including this one.
auth.accountHint: Signed in on this computer. Your rows, your workbook.
auth.mySearchHint: What you are looking for, and where
auth.signOutSure: Sign out? Your jobs and notes stay on this computer.

welcome.needSource: Pick at least one source. A search with nowhere to look finds nothing.

headline.title: What job are you after?
headline.lede: In your own words. Nothing filters on this -- it is how the app talks to you about your search, and how a cover letter opens.
headline.label: The job you want
headline.hint: For example: GIS analyst, kitchen porter, junior back-end developer.

keywords.stems: The words here are beginnings, not whole words. An ad will not say surveyor, it will say surveying technician — so survey catches both. Three or four beginnings are usually enough.
keywords.result: Ads that match go into your spreadsheet under the category
keywords.noneWarning: With no words at all, every ad from every source you pick comes through. That is a real choice — just not usually the one people mean.
keywords.halfTyped: A group with a name but no words matches nothing, and will not be saved. Give it a word, or remove it.
keywords.title: Which words mean that job?
keywords.lede: Ads do not use your title, they use theirs. Group the words that mean the same thing, and name each group -- the name is the category that lands in your spreadsheet. Groups are tried in order, and the first that matches wins.

where.title: Where would you work?
where.lede: Leave it all empty to search everywhere, which is the right answer more often than people expect.
where.locationsHint: Empty means anywhere. Location filtering is skipped entirely.
where.regionsHint: For sources that say the region rather than the town.
where.remoteHint: An ad matching one of these counts as being where you are.
where.regionsAreASecondChoice: A county is only consulted when an ad names no town at all. On one government portal the county field holds the address of the office that published the ad rather than the job — so the town, when there is one, decides.

freshness.title: How old may an ad be?
freshness.lede: This only applies to ads that carry no closing date of their own. One with a deadline is judged on the deadline.
freshness.label: Skip ads older than
freshness.hint: Thirty days suits most searches. Lower it if you are looking every day.

employers.title: Who would you work for?
employers.lede: All of this is optional and all of it can be changed later. Start typing and JobSheet offers the employers it has already seen in your own ads.
employers.dreamHint: These never filter anything out. An ad from one of them gets a ⭐ on its row, so it is the one you see first in a sheet of ninety.
employers.skipHint: Agencies you have had enough of, or a former employer.
employers.contractsHint: Tick nothing and every kind of contract comes through, which is the right answer for most searches. These are matched as beginnings, like every other word here.
employers.unstatedArePassed: An ad that does not say what contract it offers still comes through, marked. Half the sources never state it, and dropping those would cost you most of the search.
employers.schedulesHint: Night shifts, weekends, split shifts -- whatever you will not do.

sources.title: Where should JobSheet look?
sources.lede: Every one of these is a public feed or a public API. No account, no key, nothing behind a login. Pick as many as you like -- they are fetched at the same time.

workbook.title: Where should your spreadsheet live?
workbook.lede: This is the file you will actually open. Put it somewhere you look -- your Desktop is a good answer.
workbook.hint: Touch neither and JobSheet keeps the file with everything else. The name has to end in .xlsx.

landing.headline: Every ad you find, in one spreadsheet you own.
landing.lede: JobSheet checks the sources you pick, drops what you already have, and writes the rest into an .xlsx with your columns. Your ticks and your notes stay yours -- and stay on the right job when the next search re-sorts the sheet.
landing.startClaim: Take over the search that is here
landing.privacy: No account on anybody's server. Nothing leaves this computer.
landing.claimNote: There is already a search on this computer, from before JobSheet had accounts. Take it over and everything in it stays where it is.

sample.label: Roughly what lands on your desk

one.title: Say what you are after
one.body: A minute of questions: the job, the words that mean it, where you would work, and what you would rather not see again.

two.title: It looks everywhere at once
two.body: Public feeds and public APIs, fetched together. The same job posted in three places is one row, and an ad you already have does not come back.

three.title: You get a spreadsheet
three.body: A real .xlsx with the columns you chose. Tick a row in Excel, search again, and the tick is still on that job after the sheet re-sorts.

sheet.title: A file you own
sheet.body: Plain .xlsx, on your disk. No login to read it, nothing to renew, and it opens in whatever you already use.

tracker.title: Somewhere to keep track
tracker.body: New, applied, interview, offer, rejected -- a board that answers where each application stands.

letter.title: A letter to start from
letter.body: A cover letter drafted from the ad and from what you said you are after. Yours to rewrite.

local.title: Nothing leaves
local.body: Your searches, your notes and your file stay on this computer. There is no cloud behind this and no key to buy.

sources.label: Where it looks
sources.hint: Every one of these is a public feed or a public API. No account, no key, nothing behind a login -- and a new one is a plugin, not a new version of JobSheet.
sources.unknown: The list is on the sources screen, once you are inside.

closing.title: Ready when you are.
closing.body: The questions take a minute, and every answer can be changed afterwards.

home.title: Your search
home.lede: One button. Everything it needs was answered when you set this up.
home.nothingSetUp: This account has no saved search yet.
